approved_payload.content: Two men were wounded when shots were fired at the Palm taxi rank in Delft at about 07:00 on Wednesday 28 October, according to police. Police are investigating two counts of attempted murder and the discharge of a firearm, and no arrests had been made (Cape Argus, 28 Oct). Police described the shooting as between taxi drivers. Hundreds of commuters ran for cover and police closed the rank. On 29 October the Western Cape police commissioner, Sizakhele Dyantyi, told IOL that police had intelligence about a planned shooting in Delft and had officers at the rank when shots were fired from another part of it. No one was killed and no one is named. Accounts differ on small points: the Cape Times says Tuesday morning, but its police quote says 'this morning' and it was published on Wednesday 28 October, the date TygerBurger gives; the Cape Argus says the wounded went to hospital in a private vehicle, TygerBurger says by another taxi. It is the second shooting at this rank since 22 October; sharing a rank is not, on its own, a link. The map point is approximate: the rank is not mapped, so the pin is where Palm Street meets Delft Main Road, not a confirmed spot.
